reader.requirement: At --std 85 every data description entry must begin with a level-number written as a one- or two-digit number (1-9 also as 01-09), from 01-49, 66 or 88 under an FD, SD or CD and from 01-49, 66, 77 or 88 in working-storage and linkage, and anything else (a three-digit spelling, 00, 50-65, 78, 99, a signed or decimal number, a missing level) must be refused; the witness covers only the legal hierarchy.
reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|DialectLevel|IsActive over LevelNumberPass.cs: none (the class doc states the sets are the same at 85/2002/2014/2023); the CD arm is selected by parse ancestry (CommunicationDescriptionEntryContext), not by edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the legal hierarchy only; the one-digit spellings, the section sets (FD vs working-storage vs CD) and the refusal half are not exercised

probes.expected: levels 1, 2, 5, 9, 09, 49, 66, 77, 88 accepted in FD, working-storage and linkage

probes.printed: COBOL1746 level-number 77 ... subordinate to a CD entry
COBOL1746 level-number 001 ... one-digit or two-digit number
COBOL1746 level-number 77 ... subordinate to a FD or SD

reader.notes: LevelNumberPass is edition-invariant and its sets match the 1985 SR2/SR3, including the CD arm. The diagnostics cite 2023 rules (and mention local-storage) at 85, which is cosmetic.

refuter.evidence: At --std 85 vs 2023 (lv_a..lv_e.cob in E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-001/): 01 and 77 written in area B (column 12): 85 COBOL3734 'level-number 01/77 begins in area B', 2023 compiles and prints X (1985 reference format; an edition site the reader did not list, taking a correct 85 arm). lv_c.cob 01 G with 05 and one-digit 5 children in area A and a 77 after an 01 compiles and prints XYZW (cite.py OK  §1985:VI.5.7.3 SR3). Under an RD, 88 and 77 are refused COBOL1746 at both editions. Reader's refusals of 00, 001, 50, 65, 78, 99, signed/decimal and missing levels stand.
